thread:
erin: Noticed during a routing-policies demo: when switching a tenant from `route-profile:v1` -> `route-profile:v2` the Roles panel loses the per-route quota override control for some roles. UI shows "no permission" but role JSON still contains `quota:override`.
maya: Repro steps? I've been trying to break this too.
erin: Steps: 1) tenant in canary (profile v2) 2) open Console > Roles > select role that has `quota:override` 3) click route `/v1/generate` -> effective perms show false and edit disabled.
yusuf: Can you paste the API calls the console makes?
erin: Console calls `GET /api/v1/roles/:id/effective?route=/v1/generate&profile=route-profile:v2` and response includes `{"effective":{"quota:override":false}, "meta":{"profile":"route-profile:v2","computed_by":"route-eval-v2"}}` but `GET /api/v1/roles/:id` shows `permissions:["quota:override","route:read"]`.
maya: Sounds like route-eval-v2 has different semantics for profile-scoped role bindings. Maybe binding normalization changed.
sasha: I dug in. route-eval-v2 treats bindings with missing `profile` as future-compatible and maps them to `profile:default` at read-time — but the console sends `profile=route-profile:v2` which triggers a strict-match path. Effect: old tenant bindings (no explicit profile) don't match and are treated as absent.
yusuf: So migration gap: we need a read-side compatibility shim that treats missing-profile as matching any profile until we backfill bindings.
maya: UX: until we fix, we should show a banner: "Routing profile migration in progress — some effective permissions may appear stale. Click 'Ensure fresh' to check authoritative permissions." Put behind `showProfileMigrationNotice`.
erin: And add telemetry: `perm_effective.profile_mismatch` with tags {tenant, role, profile} so we can count impacted queries. Also `perm_effective.ensure_fresh_click`.
sasha: Implementation plan: 1) quick patch in route-eval-v2: if profile param present and no explicit bindings found, run compatibility matcher that treats missing-profile bindings as matches and mark `meta.compat_match=true`. 2) emit telemetry. 3) schedule backfill job to stamp explicit profiles on bindings (backfill does not change semantics).
yusuf: For data safety add a toggle: `compatProfileRead=true` in route-eval config and enable only for canary tenants first. Also add a rate-limited fallback to primary store for heavy queries to avoid full-scan.
maya: Console change: show the compatibility badge if `meta.compat_match==true` and enable an "Apply anyway" button with confirmation so users can edit quotas even if we used compat read. Also provide a link to the migration status page.
sasha: I'll open PR: services/route-eval/v2 - add compat matcher, meta.compat_match, telemetry, config toggle, unit tests.
audit-bot: audit: profile_read_compat.requested_by=erin, tenants=[canary-alpha], request_id=req_4755
yusuf: Also plan backfill: migration job templates/2026-03-25-profile-backfill that scans `role_bindings` and sets `profile=default` where NULL. We'll run with low priority and watch `backfill.progress` and `backfill.mismatch_count`.
maya: Dashboard asks: add an observability tile in Console Ops showing `perm_effective.profile_mismatch` rate, percent of roles affected, and `backfill.progress`. We'll use that to decide when to disable compat shim.
sasha: small note: add integration test that flips tenant profile, updates a binding post-backfill and verifies route-eval picks it up immediately (no stale window).
deploy-bot: queued deploy to staging (build #9754) - running unit & integration tests.
erin: Thanks. Once compat patch is up let's run a 2-hour canary and notify support. I'll prepare a short KB for support explaining the Ensure fresh workflow and how to interpret `meta.compat_match`. :white_check_mark:
